**The decision:** DEC-2026-0001, made on 2026-09-23. Sarah Chen asked for 15% off the NS-500 Industrial Controller for Acme Manufacturing (CRM-2048, ERP C-1001). The outcome was "approve with authorization," and Michael Torres approved it as VP Sales on 2026-09-24.

**Why it was valid then:**
1. **Pricing policy:** The request was dated 2026-09-23, so Northstar Pricing Policy 2026 and Approval Authority Matrix APP-MATRIX-2026 applied (both run 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31). Under them, an Enterprise Account Executive can approve up to 10%, VP Sales covers more than 10% up to 20%, and anything over 20% needs the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO).
2. **Who could approve:** Sarah Chen is an Enterprise Account Executive, so she could not approve 15% herself. The request correctly went to VP Sales.
3. **Approver's role:** The employee list and org chart both show Michael Torres as VP Sales, reporting to CRO David Morgan. Neither source dates the role, but nothing suggests he held a different one in September 2026. He has approved other VP-level discounts over time as well.
4. **Customer's contract terms:** Acme's Master Supply Agreement (ACME-MFG-2025) and its pricing exception EXC-ACME-NS500-15 both run from 2025-04-01 to 2028-03-31. The exception allows up to 15% on the NS-500 only. The request was for exactly 15% on the NS-500, so it was within the cap. The older 10% exception (EXC-ACME-NS500-10) was replaced from 2025-04-01 onward.

**One caveat about today (2027-02-01):** Pricing Policy 2027 has been in force since 2027-01-01. It lowers VP Sales authority to more than 5% up to 12%, and anything over 12% needs the CRO. A 15% discount requested today would need CRO approval. That policy only covers requests dated on or after 2027-01-01, so it doesn't change the DR-9001 decision.
